title: Claude Limitations
description: Understand Claude's honest limitations — hallucination, knowledge cutoff, context constraints, and how to work around each one.

data.text: Every AI system has limitations, and Claude is no exception. Understanding these limitations honestly is not a criticism — it is the foundation of using Claude effectively. Users who understand where Claude struggles can design workflows that avoid those pitfalls and get consistently better results.

Like all LLMs, Claude can hallucinate — it can generate plausible-sounding information that is factually incorrect. This happens most often when: Claude is asked about events after its training cutoff, it is asked for specific statistics or quotes without source material, or it is pushed to be confident about something it does not actually know. The safer you are with facts, the more you should verify Claude's claims.

data.title: Hallucination is not rare
data.text: Studies consistently show that LLMs hallucinate on factual questions 15-30% of the time, often with high confidence. Claude is among the most accurate models, but it is not immune. Always verify factual claims — especially statistics, dates, quotes, and specific details.

Claude's knowledge comes from its training data, which has a cutoff date. Claude does not know about events, products, or developments that happened after its last training update. For current events, use Perplexity or enable web browsing. For historical knowledge within the training window, Claude is generally reliable but should still be verified for critical applications.

Even Claude's large 200K context window has limits. When a conversation exceeds the context window, earlier messages 'fall off' the context and Claude loses track of them. For very long projects, start new conversations with a summary of the important context from the previous one.

data.title: Limitations to keep in mind:
items: No image generation — Claude is text-only
Limited web access — the free tier has minimal browsing capability
Cannot verify its own accuracy — it does not 'know' when it is wrong
May refuse legitimate requests due to safety training
Can be overly cautious or verbose by default
Does not have real-time data without explicit web search integration

data.title: Practical workarounds:
items: For hallucination: Always verify facts, provide source material, and ask Claude to cite its sources
For knowledge cutoff: Use Claude alongside Perplexity for current information
For context limits: Start new conversations with a context summary from the previous one
For refusals: Rephrase requests to focus on the legitimate educational or professional intent
For verbosity: Add 'be concise' or 'respond in under 200 words' to your prompt

data.title: Honest limitation assessment
data.text: Claude's limitations are well-documented and relatively predictable. Unlike some assistants that over-promise, Claude's design team is transparent about what the system can and cannot do. This honesty is itself a feature — it lets you plan around limitations rather than discovering them unexpectedly.

data.title: Understanding Claude's limits
points: Hallucination is real — always verify factual claims
Knowledge has a cutoff — use Perplexity for current events
Context window limits exist even at 200K tokens
No image generation or persistent memory across sessions
Most limitations have practical workarounds with the right prompting
